article.articleHeadline: Doctors Without Borders Urges Broader Use of Merck's Ervebo Vaccine in Bundibugyo Outbreak in Congo
article.articleSummary:
- Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo, centered on Bundibugyo, reports 10,920 confirmed infections and 5,323 deaths as of 7 November 2026 (largest Ebola outbreak in the country and second-largest globally). Doctors Without Borders (MSF) urges expanded access to Merck’s Ervebo vaccine (Zaïre ebolavirus) beyond current targets, to include more at-risk groups such as young children, despite Ervebo being developed for the Zaïre strain. Early field observations show reduced mortality and fewer confirmed infections among those vaccinated before this outbreak, suggesting possible cross-protection, though not proven against Bundibugyo. - On 2026-11-09, Doctors Without Borders (MSF) urges wider deployment of Merck’s Ebola vaccine Ervebo in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s escalating Bundibugyo outbreak, citing emerging evidence that the shot may protect against Bundibugyo ebolavirus despite being developed against the Zaire strain. Ervebo was developed against the Zaire ebolavirus strain; MSF argues broader use could bolster outbreak response given potential cross-protection. The article does not provide case or death counts, laboratory confirmation details, or specific infection sources. The emphasis remains on extending vaccine access to curb transmission in the DRC outbreak, with ongoing questions about cross-strain effectiveness.
- On 9 November 2026, African CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya urged establishing a 'peace corridor' to secure the Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), following an Islamic State–affiliated attack by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) that killed about 30 civilians in Cantine-Aloya, North Kivu, and allowed Ebola patients to flee a health center. The violence disrupts care, contact tracing, and surveillance, with hundreds of people infected or suspected fleeing for safety. Kaseya emphasized that safe access to health care and the ability of health workers to provide essential services must be protected, and called on all parties to uphold international humanitarian law protecting health care and facilities, while expressing solidarity with the DRC population.
- MSF calls for rapid expansion of access to an Ebola vaccine to tackle the Democratic Republic of Congo outbreak. More than 5,000 have died among nearly 11,000 cases, making it the deadliest Ebola outbreak in DRC history. There is no specific vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain driving this outbreak, but trials are assessing Ervebo, approved for a more common Ebola strain, for cross-protection. MSF argues expanding access could protect more at-risk people. WHO recently launched a clinical trial in the DRC to test cross-protection against Bundibugyo. Since September, MSF has been vaccinating about 20,000 frontline workers in an observational study using Ervebo. The DRC declared its 17th Ebola outbreak on May 15, with the WHO's PHEIC declaration two days later.
- UN humanitarian coordinator in the DRC, Alain Akpadji, voiced deep concern over violence since 8 November 2026 in Fataki health zone, Djugu territory, Ituri, threatening civilians and the Ebola response. In a 9 November 2026 statement, he condemned attacks on civilians and urged all parties to respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians and critical infrastructure, and facilitate aid access to save lives. On 8 November 2026, at least five civilians were injured near the Plaine Savo displacement site, with gunfire also reported in the town of Fataki about 25 km away. Ongoing insecurity has curtailed humanitarian access and suspended an in-progress needs assessment mission since late October. article.articleHeadline: Climate change is already causing an increase in infectious diseases in the country - Jornal O Sul.
article.articleSummary:
- Climate change is driving dengue expansion in Brazil, with Rio Grande do Sul registering nearly 210,000 confirmed dengue infections and 281 deaths in 2024, and Bahia about 163,000 cases and 188 deaths. A Fiocruz study (2006–2024) found epidemic dengue microregions rose from 110 to 292, representing about 54% of the country, suggesting irreversible expansion once the virus and vector are introduced. The spread tracks warmer temperature anomalies that alter mosquito biology. Dengue outbreaks are reaching cooler regions and even autochthonous cases have occurred in the continental United States; France and Italy reported autochthonous cases as well. Oropouche fever surpassed 12,000 infections in 2023 across 23 states and the Federal District. Leptospirosis spikes followed floods, notably in R
- Oropouche virus (Orthobunyavirus oropoucheense) surveillance from 1955 to early 2025 shows rapid spread beyond the Amazon with sustained transmission across South and Central America and imported infections in North America and Europe. Primary vector is Culicoides paraensis, with possible secondary vectors including Culex quinquefasciatus and several mosquitoes (Aedes serratus, Psorophora cingulata, Haemagogus tropicalis). After its 1955 isolation in Trinidad, the 1961 Belém urban outbreak (~11,000 cases) preceded Brazilian spread to Pará, Amapá, Amazonas, Maranhão and Goiás, with Brazil reporting about 500,000 infections (likely underestimated). International introductions began 1989 (Panama) and spread to Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador, Venezuela, Haiti, Colombia, French Guiana, and Cuba (2024).
- Campinas launches the 2nd Municipal Week of Mobilization to Combat Arboviruses (Aedes aegypti) from 9 to 14 November 2026 to intensify prevention and control of dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. The campaign aims to preempt vector proliferation amid climate change and El Niño, which may raise temperatures and alter rainfall. The intersectoral Municipal Arboviroses Committee coordinates actions across health, education, public works, civil defense, housing, social assistance, environment, culture, and more, with citizen and brigadista participation pivotal to eliminating breeding sites. - Barra do Piraí reports 154 dengue notifications in 2026, with 134 discarded and 20 probable cases, amid rising Aedes aegypti activity that also transmits chikungunya and zika. Environmental surveillance recorded 44,200 eggs collected by ovitrampas and found larvae predominantly in residential settings (over 80%). Over 170,000 property visits have been conducted in 2026 to identify breeding sites and direct interventions; October figures remain partial. A Ministry of Health alert warns of potential arbovirus increases in 2026–2027 linked to El Niño, with dengue impact expected to be strongest in the Southeast. - Brazil could see dengue cases rise in 2027 as a very intense El Niño influences temperature and rainfall patterns, say researchers including Fiocruz from eight countries. article.articleHeadline: Support Vector Machine Leads Prediction of Infection After Open Pulmonary
article.articleSummary: West China Hospital evaluated nine machine-learning models using 14 clinical variables to predict postoperative infection after open pulmonary lobectomy in 3,160 patients treated from 2017–2025; 369 infections occurred (11.68%). Respiratory tract infections (6.17%) and surgical site infections (5.38%) were the main complications, with deep organ/space infections comprising 70.59% of SSIs. The support vector machine showed the strongest discrimination (AUC 0.645; 95% CI 0.589–0.700), followed by random forest (0.632) and logistic regression (0.624). K-nearest neighbors had the highest accuracy (0.806) and specificity (0.887); SVM had the highest sensitivity (0.586) and negative predictive value (0.921). Random forest posted the top F1 (0.276). Calibration varied (Brier 0.156–0.241). Decision-curve analysis showed net benefit at low thresholds (0.01–0.11). SHAP highlighted age, total surgical duration, and preoperative hospital stay as key predictors across models. Conclusion: ML risk stratification using pre/intraoperative data shows potential and warrants external validation.

article.articleHeadline: Sequencing Pediatric Lung Fluid Links Microbial Load to Distinct Pneumonia
article.articleSummary: Sequencing pediatric BAL fluid links microbial load to pneumonia phenotypes. In 791 hospitalized children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China (Aug 2023–Jul 2024), researchers performed targeted next-generation sequencing on bronchoalveolar lavage to quantify DNA load, detect co-pathogens, and assess antimicrobial resistance mutations. BAL collected within 72 hours of admission; a 198-pathogen panel and resistance gene profiling interrogated macrolide-resistance mutations A2063G/A2064G. Inclusion required ages 1 month–16 years and ≥50 pathogen reads with ≥1,000 copies/mL DNA. High MP load defined as >1,000,000 copies/mL; low load 1,000–1,000,000; co-infection if any co-pathogen ≥1,000 copies/mL. Of 791, 309 monoinfection and 482 co-infection (60.9%). 652 high-load and 139 low-load cases. High-load monoinfection associated with persistent fever and localized consolidation; low-load co-infection tied to younger age, respiratory distress, wheeze, dyspnea, higher inflammatory markers, and more severe pneumonia. Background: East Asia macrolide resistance 70–90% vs 10–15% NA/Europe.

article.articleHeadline: Every Hour of Delay After an Open-Globe Injury Raises Endophthalmitis Risk,
article.articleSummary: Open-globe injury-associated endophthalmitis in central China rises with longer injury-to-admission. In 344 surgically treated patients (2017–2024) at a tertiary eye hospital, 172 developed preoperative endophthalmitis and were matched to 172 controls. Median injury-to-admission was 48.0 hours for cases (IQR 24–96) versus 8.0 hours for controls (IQR 5–12.5). Using a log2-transformed interval and propensity-score matching, each doubling of delay increased odds of endophthalmitis by 2.30 (95% CI 1.71–3.10) after adjustment for demographics and trauma factors; results were robust under multiple-imputation and complete-case analyses. The authors caution that this is a retrospective, single-center study and cannot prove causation. They frame the finding as a continuous, graded risk with delay, not a fixed cutoff, implying prompt admission reduces infection risk without identifying a safe interval.

article.articleHeadline: Even 30-year-old marathon stars are getting hit! Streptococcus pneumoniae serotype reshuffle—prevention must keep pace with the times.
article.articleSummary: World Pneumonia Day (Nov 12) in Hong Kong highlights invasive pneumococcal disease risk beyond the elderly, as a man in his 30s who regularly runs marathons developed severe invasive pneumococcal pneumonia with bacteremia due to serotype 3, required oxygen and 10–14 days in hospital, and left with lung scar and potential traction bronchiectasis. Streptococcus pneumoniae has over 100 serotypes; vaccination reshapes the serotype landscape, with serotypes 15A and 23A rising and often more antibiotic-resistant, complicating treatment though prompt antibiotics within four hours remain crucial. High-risk groups (age ≥50, children, asthma, bronchiectasis, cardiovascular disease) face greater risk of severe disease and complications such as stroke. Vaccination guidance now favors 20- or 21-valent pneumococcal vaccines; 21-valent covers emerging 15A and 23A strains and replaces some older ones. In Hong Kong (2025 data), subsidies target elderly/high-risk; all ages can vaccinate (self-pay or vouchers); co-vaccinate with influenza before autumn-winter peak.

article.articleHeadline: Surveillance Reveals HIV-1 Drug Resistance Patterns and Risk Factors in
article.articleSummary: From 2022–2024 in Huzhou, China, a surveillance of HIV-1 antiretroviral therapy (ART) failure involving 184 patients found 81 (44.0%) with acquired drug resistance mutations. NNRTI resistance occurred in 41.8% of patients, with dominant mutations V179D/E/F, K103N, V106I/L/M, G190A/Q/S/T, and Y181C/L. NRTI resistance was present in 27.7%, most frequently M184V/I and K65R. PI resistance remained low at 1.6%. Multivariable analysis identified age, higher plasma viral load, and specific HIV-1 subtypes as independent risk factors for resistance mutations. Viral pol region sequencing, interpreted via the Stanford HIV Drug Resistance Database, underpinned these findings. The study characterizes an evolving mutational landscape among ART-experienced individuals and provides evidence to optimize personalized ART regimens and reduce onward transmission of drug-resistant HIV-1 in the region.

article.articleHeadline: Health Security At Risk: How Climate Change Spawns The Next Epidemic
article.articleSummary: Climate instability is identified as a primary driver of emerging infectious diseases, with habitat fragmentation and shifting wildlife ranges elevating spillover risk. Panel at Sustainability Expo 2026 (November 7) warned that permafrost thaw in Siberia risks reactivating dormant pathogens, and that warming accelerates breeding of Aedes and Anopheles vectors, expanding vector-borne illnesses into new regions. The 1998 Nipah outbreak in Malaysia is cited as a canonical example of how environmental destruction triggers crises; during a severe El Niño in Indonesia, loss of habitat and fruit bat migration led to Nipah entering pig populations and then farm workers. More than 100 human deaths from encephalitis and respiratory distress; about 1.2 million pigs culled to curb transmission. WHO Thailand advocates treating climate change as a public health crisis; emphasis on proactive surveillance, rapid data sharing, education, and disaster-resilient health infrastructure, with genomic diagnostics enabling near real-time responses.

Virologist Yong Poovorawan, WHO Thailand representative Dr. Alisa Yanasarn, and environmental health expert Sonthi Kochawat outlined three pathways: expanding vectors like mosquitoes, altered animal–human contact, and thawing permafrost exposing long-dormant pathogens. Dengue, malaria, and Zika—driven by temperature and rainfall—could reach new areas, though outbreaks depend on public health measures and local conditions. They cited Russia’s 2016 anthrax outbreak to illustrate exposure risks from heat and permafrost, but cautioned not all ancient microbes threaten humans. WHO estimates climate change may cause about 250,000 additional deaths annually (2030–2050) from malnutrition, malaria, diarrhea, and heat injuries. Calls for integrated environmental monitoring, disease surveillance, and stronger disaster-ready healthcare, especially for pregnant women, children, and outdoor workers.

article.articleHeadline: Influenza A H1N1 Dominates Thailand as Cases Surge
article.articleSummary: Thailand's influenza surveillance shows Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 dominating October, accounting for 115 of 122 lab-confirmed flu infections (94.3%) from 581 specimens tested. For January–October 2026, 8,734 samples were analyzed with 1,278 positives (positivity 14.63%); H1N1pdm09 caused 704 cases (55.09%), followed by A(H3N2) with 306 (23.94%) and Influenza B Victoria lineage with 268 (20.97%). Genomic data indicate H1N1pdm09 subclade 6B.1A.5a.2a.1 as the principal circulating group; H3N2 is dominated by the K clade, and B by V1A.3a.2. Antiviral resistance testing of 127 October specimens found no known resistance mutations, including absence of H275Y linked to oseltamivir. Officials urge continued genomic surveillance, vaccination, hygiene, early clinical assessment, and ongoing monitoring given rapid subtype shifts and potential resistance emergence.

article.articleHeadline: Comparison of stool examination, urine rapid diagnostic test (RDT), and stool PCR for diagnosing Opisthorchis viverrini infection
article.articleSummary: In a northern Thai correctional facility where Opisthorchis viverrini and Haplorchis taichui are co-endemic and residents had avoided raw fish for at least one month, 239 men were evaluated using single stool specimens (Kato-Katz and PBS-ethyl acetate concentration) with ITS2-PCR as the reference standard. PCR detected O. viverrini in 6.7% (16/239). Urine rapid diagnostic testing (OV-RDT) was positive in 77.0% (124/161) of participants with valid urine. Against PCR, OV-RDT sensitivity was 75.0% (95% CI 42.8–94.5) and specificity 22.8% (95% CI 16.3–30.4); likelihood ratios near one, and band intensity did not distinguish PCR status. Specificity remained low under composite references and among those with no helminths detected (21.3%). Taenia spp. were found in 12.1% but were not associated with OV-RDT positivity. Conclusion: OV-RDT positivity poorly reflects molecular infection in this low-prevalence, co-endemic setting, underscoring the need for confirmatory testing before using OV-RDT results for prevalence estimates or treatment decisions.

article.articleHeadline: Melioidosis Antibody Response Persists Years After Infection
article.articleSummary: Melioidosis antibody responses persist for years after infection, according to a Lancet Microbe retrospective cohort study from UC Davis and Mahidol University. In Thailand, researchers followed individuals after confirmed Burkholderia pseudomallei infection and found antibody levels against two diagnostic targets remained detectable long term, meaning positive antibody tests may reflect past exposure rather than current disease. Melioidosis, a serious infection transmitted through contact with soil and surface water contaminated with Burkholderia pseudomallei, causes fever, stomach pain, seizures and has a 10–50% fatality rate. Historically endemic in northern Australia and Southeast Asia (notably northeast Thailand), its geographic range appears expanding; in 2022 the CDC linked human cases in Mississippi to soil and water, signaling establishment in the continental US, with rising reports in South Asia and Africa. Climate change may broaden suitable environments, underscoring need for surveillance and clinician awareness.

article.articleHeadline: Study Identifies Key Predictors of Adverse Tuberculosis Outcomes in
article.articleSummary: Retrospective analysis of Ni-kshay records from Maharashtra, India, 2021–2022 identified predictors of adverse outcomes in adult drug-sensitive TB. The unfavourable-outcome cohort included 323,124 cases; the mortality cohort included 315,579. Increased age, male gender, lower pre-treatment weight, tobacco use, and alcohol consumption significantly raised odds of unfavourable outcomes and death; HIV and diabetes also increased risk. Records with missing data for behavioral risks or comorbidities (unknown) likewise carried higher odds. Using multivariable logistic regression, baseline adjustment for age, gender, and weight, and treating missing data as a category, with collinearity checked via Cramer's V and VIF. The study demonstrates the utility of routine digital health data to flag high-risk TB patients and guide state-level interventions in a country that accounts for about one-quarter of global TB cases. TB remains the leading infectious cause of death worldwide.

article.articleHeadline: Chong Kun Dang Gochon Foundation Awards Kochon Prize to Three TB Eradication Groups
article.articleSummary: On 9 November 2026, the Chong Kun Dang Gochon Foundation announced three organizations—Marshall Islands Tuberculosis Management Program (Marshall Islands), India's REACH, and Kenya's Health Solution Center—as joint recipients of the 20th Kochon Prize for their contributions to global tuberculosis eradication. They were recognized for establishing integrated screening systems that test tuberculosis and other diseases simultaneously, enabling early TB detection and improving access to treatment for patients. The Kochon Prize, established in 2006, honors outstanding contributions to tuberculosis eradication and underscores international efforts to advance TB control through multiplex screening in diverse settings. These programs demonstrate scalable models for early detection and treatment access in the Marshall Islands, India, and Kenya, highlighting cross-national collaboration in tuberculosis prevention and care.

article.articleHeadline: Spatiotemporal Study Reveals Shifting Malaria Clusters Across Districts in
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Assam, India (2011–2023) shows a substantial statewide decline but persistent, highly focal transmission with clusters in forested border districts and central hill tracts. Across 27 baseline districts (aligned to the 2011 Census), 147,007 cases were recorded. Adults over 15 years bore the majority of the burden (90,801 cases; 61.8%), with males most affected; school-age children (5–14) had the highest relative incidence, while under-5s had lower absolute counts. Rural residents (84.2%) live in flood-prone, monsoonal Assam (≈36.16 million people; 78,438 sq km), where standing water sustains vectors amid historic Plasmodium falciparum malaria, land-use pressures, insecticide/drug resistance, and limited healthcare access. The study used SaTScan cluster detection and Bayesian INLA modeling, finding zero-inflated Poisson models fit best, underscoring ongoing local transmission despite overall decline.

article.articleHeadline: Gita Karmakar: The nurse Jalpaiguri knew as Polio Didimoni
article.articleSummary: Gita Karmakar, known as Polio Didimoni, served Jalpaiguri’s Danguajhar tea garden area in north-west West Bengal from 1983 as an auxiliary nurse midwife, later field nurse. She covered 12–14 km daily, mostly by bicycle, running clinics, promoting hospital births (about 100 per year), weighing children, monitoring nutrition, and maintaining the vaccine cold chain while teaching about tuberculosis, thalassemia and reproductive health. She became a familiar figure during polio campaigns, earning the nickname Polio Didimoni. After a 2008 road accident left 40% disability, she hired a cycle-rickshaw to continue visiting patients, paying about 200 rupees daily. In January 2021 she was promoted to Health Supervisor at Belakoba Rural Hospital, guiding 33 ASHA workers across four health centres. She retired on 31 January 2026, had been nominated for the National Florence Nightingale Award, and on 12 May 2026 received the award from the President at Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi, marking International Nurses Day.

article.articleHeadline: Nipah will recur in Kerala; Former Health Department Secretary issues a warning.
article.articleSummary: Nipah virus is expected to recur in Kerala, says former Health Department Secretary Rajeev Sadanandan. He estimates up to 50% of flying-fox fruit bats (Pteropus spp.) could carry Nipah, and that dense population with increasing human–animal contact heightens spillover risk. Bats can transmit without dying, allowing ongoing spread; earlier studies found about 22% of bats infected, supporting annual Nipah cases beyond Kozhikode. Nipah is not confined to one district; in 2019 Idukki reported a case. Kerala’s transparent reporting has drawn attention, while some regions may underreport. In 2018, recognizing the outbreak’s spread took about 18 days; mortality could reach 70–100%. Malabar projections suggested up to 254 cases with preparations for 300 patients, hampered by PPE shortages. Two lessons: strengthen disease surveillance and hospital infection control; and ensure Nipah testing for youths with brain-related symptoms, as gaps led to about 13 related infections.

KNR company, responsible for the drains, stated mud accumulation after completion could cause the issue and promised immediate cleaning and arrangements to allow rainwater runoff to reduce mosquito breeding.

article.articleHeadline: Fern Extract Produces Silver Nanoparticles That Eliminate Disease-Carrying
article.articleSummary: Biogenic silver nanoparticles were synthesized by reducing silver nitrate with aqueous leaf extract of Adiantum latifolium collected from Thiruvananthapuram district, Kerala, India. Formation confirmed by surface plasmon resonance at 414 nm; X-ray diffraction matched FCC structure (JCPDS 04-0783); FTIR indicated phytochemicals such as flavones, terpenoids, reducing sugars capping the particles. The nanoparticles exhibited potent larvicidal activity against third-instar Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus within a 3-hour exposure. Beyond vector control, the extract and nanoparticles showed antibacterial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens and antifungal activity against Aspergillus niger and Candida albicans. Safety tests on non-target aquatic organisms and human red blood cells showed negligible toxicity. Context: dengue affects about 3.9 billion people at risk with ~390 million infections annually, and Aedes spp. are primary vectors; rising insecticide resistance drives search for plant-based, eco-friendly alternatives.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue second time: Doctor reveals why it can be more severe and shares warning signs to watch for
article.articleSummary: Dengue can be more severe on a second infection, says Mumbai infectious-disease specialist Dr. Harshad Limaye. India has all four serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4); prior infection provides serotype-specific immunity but not protection against others. In a second infection with a different type, antibodies from the first illness can enhance viral entry into immune cells (antibody-dependent enhancement, ADE), potentially raising viral load and severity, though not all second infections become severe. Severe dengue may involve plasma leakage that can accumulate fluid in the lungs or abdomen, leading to dengue shock syndrome. A falling fever does not signal recovery; watch for persistent vomiting, abdominal pain, rapid breathing, bleeding from gums or nose, fatigue or restlessness, and reduced urination. Prevention includes removing stagnant water around homes, workplaces, and construction sites, plus seeking immediate medical care if dengue symptoms appear.

article.articleHeadline: Color-changing coronavirus has returned again! The new variant PJ.2.1 has heightened concerns; WHO has issued a stern warning.
article.articleSummary: As of 9 November 2026, the SARS-CoV-2 variant PJ.2.1 has drawn a WHO warning. Infections with PJ.2.1 may resemble common cold or influenza, with symptoms such as sore throat and prolonged fatigue, making diagnosis by symptoms alone unreliable. Diagnostic testing is the most accurate method to identify PJ.2.1 and guide patient care and public health decisions. Russian infectious disease specialist Elena Malinikova notes severe throat pain and longer-lasting fatigue as possible features, though these are not exclusive to this variant. In India, vigilance remains due to earlier COVID-19 surges and overlap with winter illnesses; individuals with fever, severe sore throat, cough, or unusual fatigue should seek medical advice and undergo testing if appropriate. WHO continues global monitoring; no confirmed new global pandemic or new wave in India at present.

article.articleHeadline: Scoping review maps mucormycosis risks across diabetes and COVID-19
article.articleSummary: Rhino-orbital-cerebral mucormycosis (ROCM) is mapped across four subgroups: diabetic patients with COVID-19, diabetic without COVID, non-diabetic with COVID, and non-diabetic without COVID. In 258 patients drawn from 155 studies (124 case reports, 31 case series) published between 2010 and August 2025, Asia, led by India, accounted for the majority of cases. Diabetes mellitus was the most common comorbidity (70.9%), with prior COVID-19 in 38.4%. Early presentation featured nonspecific sinonasal symptoms; black eschar was rare (0–9.2%). Ocular involvement was frequent, with ophthalmoplegia: 55.3% in diabetics with COVID versus 35.7% without. Radiology using the Ebaid classification showed most cases at Stage IV–V (orbital to skull base/brain). Treatments combined surgical debridement with systemic antifungal therapy, predominantly liposomal amphotericin B, with posaconazole or isavuconazole as alternatives. Mortality ranged 44.3–64.3%, highest in non-diabetic, COVID-associated cases (64.3%). Evidence is descriptive, underscoring need for earlier detection and standardized staging.

article.articleHeadline: This dangerous disease troubling dengue patients could prove costly if ignored.
article.articleSummary: Dengue in India continues to surge, with Delhi at the center of concern. Across Delhi, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Kolkata, dengue cases rise after the monsoon, with liver-related problems reported among patients. In Delhi, doctors say 6–10 dengue admissions daily, and most patients are aged 20–40. Capillary leak syndrome—where plasma leaks into surrounding tissues causing swelling and a rise in blood pressure—emerges as a major complication; without timely treatment it can be fatal. Early dengue symptoms highlighted include irritability, fatigue, abdominal pain, muscle aches, excessive thirst, and sudden weight gain. The outbreak has affected thousands and led to several deaths across states. As of 9 November 2026, dengue remains a significant public health challenge in India, underscoring the need for early recognition and timely medical care to prevent progression to capillary leak and liver complications.

article.articleHeadline: Increase in Influenza A Cases Amid Poor Air Quality
article.articleSummary: Influenza A cases rose in Sept 2026 across Indonesia, with 1,527 influenza-positive results through week 3 and the highest counts in DKI Jakarta, West Java, and Banten. Sentinel surveillance found 148 of 265 samples positive (56%), but officials say this does not reflect population-wide incidence and the rise is not categorized as a large surge, still following seasonal patterns. Drivers cited include seasonal transition, increased mobility, and predominance of Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09. Regional trends mirrored Southeast Asia, with Brunei’s positivity rising from ~12% to 28% and Vietnam from ~7% to 20% by Sept 10. Air quality context shows Jakarta’s 2025 average PM2.5 at 34.1 µg/m³ (WHO guideline 5 µg/m³), suggesting a potential link between air pollution and influenza, though causality is not proven. Supporting evidence includes a 2025 meta-analysis by Ava Orr et al. showing PM2.5 exposure raises influenza risk (about 4% in adults 18–64; up to 29% in hot, dry conditions), and Indonesian pediatric studies indicating higher respiratory infections with higher PM2.5 exposure (Jakarta Barat vs Bandung) though results vary in significance.

article.articleHeadline: West Papua Health Office: Three regencies enter high malaria endemicity - ANTARA News Central Papua
article.articleSummary: West Papua Province Health Office reports 8,234 confirmed malaria cases from January–August 2026, with three of seven regencies in high endemicity: Manokwari (3,702 cases; API 11.14 per 1,000), Teluk Wondama (2,063; API 29.97), and Manokwari Selatan (1,204; API 21.3). The other regencies—Teluk Bintuni (632; API 3.86), Kaimana (366; API 4.14), Fakfak (248; API 1.44)—are moderate. Authorities are coordinating cross-regional control strategies, including border areas with Sorong Selatan (Papua Barat Daya) to curb transmission, given mobility in Kamundan and Kalitami. Pegunungan Arfak remains an elimination area. Nationwide, Indonesia recorded 706,297 malaria cases in 2025, up ~30% from 2024, with six Papua provinces contributing about 674,046 cases. Achieving the national malaria elimination target for 2030 requires intensified cross-provincial cooperation across Papua regions.

article.articleHeadline: Venezuela presents to PAHO progress toward malaria eradication.

Venezuela detailed diverse strategies and methodological innovations implemented to accelerate vector elimination. With this balance, Venezuela reaffirms commitment to global health goals, underscoring that community-led action is the most effective instrument to eradicate malaria from the country.

article.articleHeadline: Butantan uses fungus to kill schistosome larvae.
article.articleSummary: Butantan researchers repurposed the fungus Aspergillus tubingensis as a living nano‑factory to synthesize silver nanoparticle coatings that kill 100% of Schistosoma mansoni cercariae within two hours. The work, published in Environmental Science Nano, has a patent granted by INPI. Schistosomiasis is endemic in Brazil, notably the Northeast, Minas Gerais, and Espírito Santo, with freshwater snails as the intermediate host; cercariae penetrate human skin, causing chronic disease with anemia and hepatic fibrosis in underserved communities. The fungus acts as a bio‑reactor, producing biomolecules that form a protective coating around silver ions, enabling slow, targeted release and reduced environmental toxicity. Tests showed low concentrations kill cercariae, while zebrafish, microcrustaceans, and other fish exhibit far less sensitivity (microcrustaceans require 22× higher doses). The nanoparticle also targets snail embryonic stages more than adults and proved effective against Aedes aegypti larvae, highlighting a One Health, green nanotechnology approach. Field trials and a production chain are needed for real‑world deployment.

article.articleHeadline: Toads and lizards use heat as a weapon against infections - Boca do Povo News
article.articleSummary: Brazilian researchers from the University of São Paulo (USP) and the Universidade Estadual Paulista (Unesp) report that toads and lizards employ behavioral fever to fight bacterial infections. In environments with greater thermal variation, these amphibians and reptiles increase body temperature more when exposed to pathogens, with amphibians showing stronger fever responses than reptiles. The study observed higher temperature rises in animals facing bacterial challenges, indicating heat as a natural defense mechanism. However, the strategy has limits: dehydration risk for amphibians and reptiles already living near its thermal tolerance boundary. Findings published in Proceedings of the Royal Society B highlight that heat-based defenses depend on environmental conditions. This work underscores the role of behavioral thermoregulation in wildlife immunity and cautions about potential trade-offs with hydration and thermal stress in varying climates.

article.articleHeadline: Nine more dengue cases reported in Oaxaca
article.articleSummary: Nine more dengue cases were reported in Oaxaca, Mexico, during epidemiological week 43, bringing the state’s total to 80 cases and two deaths. This level remains far below 2025’s 219 cases and three deaths in the same period; after high transmission in 2024, Oaxaca saw a marked decline starting in 2025 that continues into 2026. To further reduce dengue, Oaxaca’s Health Services (SSO) announced a worldwide biocontrol strategy using Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes. The initiative, a collaboration with Universidad Autónoma de Yucatán and supported by the National Center for Prevention and Control of Diseases (CENAPRECE), will release Wolbachia egg capsules to block virus transmission, potentially cutting dengue transmission by up to 80%. Endorsed by WHO and PAHO, it is part of the National Dengue Prevention Plan and is already deployed in Yucatán, Campeche, Baja California Sur, as well as Australia, Brazil, and Indonesia. Preventive measures—repellent, screens, cleaning, and removing standing water—remain essential.

article.articleHeadline: Piauí Earns International Recognition With WHO Silver Seal for the Elimination of Vertical Transmission of Hepatitis B.
article.articleSummary: Piauí earned the World Health Organization (WHO) Silver Seal for elimination of vertical transmission of Hepatitis B, the first entity in the state to receive the recognition, acknowledged by WHO, PAHO and Brazil’s Ministry of Health. Amelia Costa, SES epidemiology coordinator, notes that while the Silver Seal is achieved, the goal remains to attain Gold and full elimination. Cristiana Rocha emphasizes positive results and plans to extend recognition to other health areas.

article.articleSummary: Rio de Janeiro again raises mpox alert as INI/Fiocruz releases a new epidemiological bulletin analyzing institute-reported diseases. The first-half 2026 panorama shows mpox notifications and a historical comparison to 2022, the year mpox emerged among the institute’s top 10 notifiable conditions. The report highlights an express change in the profile of sexually transmitted infections cared for at INI, driven by its inclusion in the sentinel surveillance network. A long-running series from 2017 through 2025 traces fluctuations in TB, syphilis, and arboviruses, marking the chikungunya era before the recent dengue peak, and documents the investigation of a suspected case of high-severity hemorrhagic fever. The complete bulletin, including the notification rankings and detailed historical analysis, is published in SEVS 2026.1.

article.articleHeadline: Tecpar establishes a national antigen bank to bolster the fight against foot-and-mouth disease
article.articleSummary: Paraná's Instituto de Tecnologia do Paraná (Tecpar), with Brazil's Ministry of Agriculture (Mapa) and Argentina's Biogénesis Bagó, established Brazil's first national antigen bank for emergency response to foot-and-mouth disease (FMD). The facility stores frozen antigens for two FMD virus serotypes, enabling production of up to 10 million vaccine doses and immediate delivery of up to 10 million doses for emergencies. Vaccines can be made available within 72 hours to the Agriculture Ministry. The bank strengthens Brazil's sanitary status as FMD-free without vaccination, recognized by the World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE) in 2025; Paraná has held this status since 2021. Antigen shelf life is about eight years, longer than vaccines, reducing stockpile needs. Tecpar becomes the sole public Brazilian lab maintaining an FMD antigen and vaccine bank, with ongoing international cooperation to enable technology transfer.

No outbreak is declared.

article.articleHeadline: Artificial intelligence advances in the diagnosis of pediatric tuberculosis.
article.articleSummary: TBPed, a multicenter Brazilian study led by Hospital Moinhos de Vento under PROADI-SUS, develops a machine-learning model to identify pediatric tuberculosis signals on chest radiographs. The project addresses diagnostic challenges in children under 15, where low bacillary load and sampling difficulties hamper confirmation and radiograph interpretation is constrained by limited sensitivity and few trained readers. Involving 27 centers across Brazil, 2,068 participants were enrolled: 1,288 hospitalized and 780 ambulatory. Among hospitalized, 54 TB diagnoses (41 laboratory-confirmed, 13 presumptive); among ambulatory, 143 TB diagnoses (38 lab-confirmed, 105 presumptive). The model trained on 2,068 chest X-rays (2,011 after quality control), with 197 TB cases (79 lab-confirmed, 118 presumptive). Internal AUROC: 0.744 (0.704–0.779). External validation: Brazil/public datasets AUROC 0.854; Peru 0.847; Cape Town, South Africa 0.543. Next steps: real-world validation and comparison with radiologists and large-language models to translate into a usable clinical tool as of 2026-11-09.

article.articleHeadline: International Workshop Highlights Community Engagement to Control Aedes
article.articleSummary: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil hosted an international workshop in September 2025 on Strengthening North-South research cooperation in social sciences for protecting vulnerable populations from Aedes-borne diseases. It underscored that community engagement and social dynamics are central determinants of effective, equitable vector control for dengue, chikungunya, and zika transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, a threat intensified by climate change, rapid urbanisation, social inequalities, and weak public infrastructures. Technical vector-control innovations (e.g., Wolbachia and sterile insect techniques) require strong social science integration, local ownership, and adaptive governance to be sustainable. Case studies from Latin America, Africa, and Europe highlighted trust, locally grounded knowledge, participatory governance, and intersectoral collaboration; citizen science, participatory surveillance, and co-designed interventions improve data quality and acceptability of innovations, empowering communities to address structural exposure determinants. Integrating social sciences into One Health is essential for resilient, inclusive responses to arboviral threats.

article.articleHeadline: Suspected human scabies leads to suspension of classes at a school in Vespasiano.
article.articleSummary: Suspected human scabies leads to school suspension in Vespasiano, Minas Gerais. Escola Municipal de Ensino Especial Vovó Mariquita suspended classes until Nov 11 after confirmation of one scabies case. Health and Education secretariats ordered preventive measures for students, staff, and families; classes will resume on Nov 12. As of 2026, the state health secretariat reports 11 scabies outbreaks in Minas Gerais, in Alfenas, Andradas, Belo Horizonte, Campos Gerais, Coronel Xavier Chaves, Itapecerica, Joaquim Felício, Lagoa Santa, Lavras, Paraguaçu, and São Gonçalo do Pará. Scabies is a skin disease caused by a mite, with intense itching and lesions. Transmission occurs mainly via prolonged skin-to-skin contact; sharing clothes, towels, or bedding can spread it. Hygiene is not the cause, and it is not spread by coughing or sneezing. Seek health care if symptoms appear; close contacts should be treated if advised; no preventive medication, and return to school depends on professionals’ guidance.

article.articleHeadline: Congo, at least 30 hippos killed by anthrax: alarm in Virunga National Park.
article.articleSummary: Anthrax outbreak in Virunga National Park, Democratic Republic of the Congo, has killed at least 30 hippopotamuses. The infections were first detected in September and confirmed by laboratory analyses, with cases concentrated around Ishango and along the Semliki River. Bacillus anthracis is the causative agent; the bacterium forms spores that can persist in the environment for years, complicating elimination. This event follows a prior outbreak within roughly a year that caused about 65 hippo deaths. Park authorities report no new cases in the past two weeks but continue active surveillance, safe carcass handling, and secure disposal to protect wildlife and human health. Drought is noted as a contributing factor, though recent rains are seen as improving the situation. The outbreak poses a zoonotic risk, and local communities are urged not to touch or consume infected carcasses.

article.articleHeadline: South Region/Rumonge: The threat of Ebola virus disease is very real.
article.articleSummary: Rumonge, Burundi faces a real threat of Ebola virus disease as clandestine entries along Lake Tanganyika risk cross-border introduction from the Democratic Republic of Congo. Six entry points were identified in Kigwena, Gatete, Rumonge, Kizuka and Minago, where nocturnal crossings by small pirogues bypass medical controls. During an Oct 28, 2026 workshop led by Edouard Ndayikengurukiye of the Public Health Emergency Operations Center, participants were briefed on transmission, Ebola symptoms, and the disease’s global and African footprint, plus Burundi’s prevention efforts. Three suspected cases in Rumonge underwent laboratory testing, all negative. Health workers asked for personal protective equipment, a request approved with the reminder that community health workers should not touch Ebola patients. A multisector mobilization—administrative authorities, health workers, religious groups, and media—was urged to ensure medical screening for all entrants and to improve information dissemination; some residents report a lack of Ebola information.

article.articleHeadline: Trump sons-linked firm landed nearly $40M in federal contracts to screen for Ebola
article.articleSummary: On 2026-11-09, XpresTest, the biosecurity unit of XWELL, was awarded nearly $40 million in U.S. government contracts to screen for Ebola at several airports and to respond to outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where Ebola has killed more than 5,000 this year. The awards—$20 million under the State Department’s America First Global Health Strategy and $18.8 million from the CDC—mark sevenfold growth from the company’s prior federal contracting. XpresTest has extensive airport COVID-19 screening experience but no Ebola or international biosecurity experience; CEO Ezra Ernst called the Congo assignment risky and unproven. Critics, including former USAID official Jeremy Konyndyk, questioned awarding a major Africa program to a firm with no Africa track record. The Trump sons are passive minority investors via American Ventures in Dominari Holdings.

article.articleHeadline: North Kivu: targeted Ebola response in Beni's priority zones - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease is the focus in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with the Beni health zone identified as the outbreak epicenter. A provincial coordination meeting on November 9, 2026, recommended concentrating response efforts in priority (hot) health areas within Beni, which comprises 26 health areas, including Bundji, Kanzuli-nzuli, Butsili, Mabolio, Mukulya, and Malepe. Authorities urged daily monitoring and investigation into drivers of resurgence to tailor interventions. Communications on risk and community engagement (CREC) face field difficulties, with emphasis on dialogue with communities. Morgue capacity constraints were acknowledged, with palliative measures under consideration. The government also invoked service minimum requirements in North-Kivu public administrations, to be implemented this week. The article highlights the Ebola outbreak in eastern DRC and ongoing efforts to curb transmission across Beni.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Mambasa: 53 private health facilities commit to strengthening screening - ACP
article.articleSummary: On 9 November 2026, Ebola response efforts in Mambasa, Ituri Province, northeast Democratic Republic of the Congo, saw 53 private health facilities commit to strengthening screening and rapid referral for suspected cases. The facilities agreed to implement a triage system—even without dedicated rooms—to take temperatures and ensure handwashing on arrival, with the aim of early detection and reducing prolonged stays before transfer to Ebola Treatment Centers (CTEs). Managers also pledged to apply the case definitions more consistently to refine referrals and to reinforce protection of mattresses in their premises as part of infection prevention. Field challenges include some patients refusing transfer to specialized centers, preferring other clinics. Dr. Yunga Abedi emphasized a collective effort with private structures and the population, calling for broad social adherence to defeat the outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: Upper Uele Province: the provincial governor on a mission to raise awareness about Ebola in Yambenda - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola awareness drive led by Haut-Uele Governor Jean Bakomito in Yambenda, Isiro, 9 November 2026. The governor conducted an on-the-ground outreach in Bavabazowa groupement, Wamba territory, to reinforce the Ebola virus disease (EVD) response following alerts from provincial elected officials and traditional chiefs about the situation in Yambenda. He urged residents not to vandalize ambulances, Ebola treatment centers (CTEs), or other response infrastructure. He pledged to strengthen the response by mobilizing additional physicians to ensure better patient care and to curb transmission. He also announced the construction of a hospital center and a school in Yambenda, aligning with the president's quinquennial education priority. On security, Bakomito cautioned the public to stay vigilant and not engage in destabilizing activities. The report does not mention confirmed cases or fatalities.

Central African Republic fears cross-border spillover. The FRN reportedly led by former president Joseph Kabila was condemned in absentia in September 2025 to death for treason, war crimes, and collaboration with M23, and faces U.S. sanctions. Economically, Kinshasa secured 45 hectares at Kwala near Dar es-Salaam for a dry port to receive, store, process and clear minerals and other goods; construction is expected to start in 2027, part of closer Tanzania–DRC ties to access the Indian Ocean.

article.articleHeadline: News | Kasaï-Central: The CNDH warns about a health crisis at Kananga prison after a death and the escape of 22 minors | mediacongo.net.
article.articleSummary: Kananga Central Prison in Kasaï-Central, Democratic Republic of the Congo, is facing a humanitarian and health crisis, according to the National Human Rights Commission (CNDH). Insufficient food, inadequate medical care, and limited access to potable water are reported, with only one of four water pumps functioning partially, worsening hygiene and disease risk. The CNDH notes the death of a prisoner with tuberculosis amid these conditions, underscoring the need for regular anti-tuberculosis treatment and adequate nutrition. In October 2026, 22 minors escaped during Oct 8–9, raising security and protection concerns for juvenile detainees. The CNDH urges urgent action from governmental, judicial, health, and provincial authorities to ensure sufficient food, consistent medical care, and reliable water supply to prevent further deaths and deteriorating conditions at Kananga’s central prison.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Washington requires travelers to spend 21 days outside the DRC before allowing boarding to the United States.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo triggers temporary U.S. travel restrictions. As of 9 November 2026, the CDC requires that travelers who have stayed in the DRC within the 21 days before departure, including those who only transited through a DRC airport, are barred from boarding flights to the United States. The rule applies to all travelers, including U.S. citizens, to reduce the risk of importing Ebola. The U.S. Embassy in Brazzaville disseminated the alert. Travelers denied boarding are advised to email [email protected] for assistance; correspondents should provide full name, date of birth, nationalities, contact details, passport details, flight information, and dates and locations of stays in RDC, Uganda, and South Sudan. The measure is described as temporary, with guidance for financial or consular assistance and lodging arrangements in a third country.

article.articleHeadline: WHO / DRC EBOLA DIGNIFIED BURIALS
article.articleSummary: On 05 October 2026 in Jina, Fataki Health Zone, Ituri Province, DRC, WHO-supported Safe and Dignified Burial teams responded to a community death alert from Ebola. Teams explained the dignified burial process to the family, obtained consent, and, after donning full protective gear, secured the body in a body bag following swab collection for testing. The coffin was prepared and carried to the cemetery for burial, with team members undressing after sealing the coffin. The operation included disinfection of entrances and engagement with residents. Medical Director Dr. Danny Byaruhanga emphasized that community awareness led to acceptance of trained teams, helping to break the transmission chain. A father of a child who died from Ebola expressed relief that the burial was conducted by professionals. The report highlights ongoing Ebola-related SDB activities in Jina to reduce infection risk.

article.articleHeadline: Is it dangerous for children to be infected with multiple respiratory viruses at the same time?
article.articleSummary: An 8-month-old in Ho Chi Minh City with concurrent RSV and Rhinovirus infection does not automatically imply greater severity than a single-virus infection. Co-infection can raise the risk of bronchiolitis, pneumonia, or respiratory failure if inflammation progresses, but severity depends on the pathogen, airway injury, and the child’s age and health. Infants under one year, especially premature babies or those with congenital heart disease, chronic lung disease, or immunodeficiency, are at higher risk of complications. Most cases are managed with supportive care: hydration, nasal suction, and close monitoring; antibiotics only for suspected bacterial infection. Seek urgent care for rapid breathing, chest retractions, poor feeding, lethargy, or cyanosis. Prevention: minimize exposure to sick contacts, avoid tobacco smoke, and follow vaccination schedules (influenza, pneumococcus, RSV, pertussis). Dr. Vo Thi Minh Tuyền, Tam Anh General Hospital, District 8.

article.articleHeadline: African swine fever in Dak Lak Province develops in a complex manner.
article.articleSummary: African swine fever (ASF) in Dak Lak Province, Vietnam, remains highly active as of early November 2026, devastating smallholder herds. Since January, ASF has affected 279 households across 46 communes, with over 11,600 pigs dead or culled, and nearly 650 tons of pork removed. In October and early November, 27 households across seven communes (Ea Súp, Ea Bung, Krông Ana, Ea Khăl, Ea Kiết, Cuôr Đăng, Ea Kao) reported outbreaks, totaling more than 350 pigs dead or culled and about 20 tons of weight. Twenty communes still have outbreaks not yet 21 days free of disease, indicating ongoing risk, especially for small-scale producers. Authorities are intensifying surveillance, controlling pig movement and sales, enforcing timely culling and disinfection, and cracking down on violations such as hidden infections and illicit transport, while promoting strict biosecurity and caution against restocking until conditions are safe.

article.articleHeadline: Buffalo and Cattle Die in Large Numbers from Unknown Causes in a Mountainous Commune in Nghệ An Province.
article.articleSummary: Unknown-cause cattle losses continue in the mountainous Hữu Kiệm commune of Nghệ An Province, Vietnam. By noon on 9 November 2026, 48 head of cattle and buffalo belonging to 17 households had died, with over 10 additional deaths reported that day. Local veterinary authorities, with the commune’s agricultural association, have visited affected areas to implement control measures and advise farmers on prevention. The Nghệ An Department of Livestock and Veterinary Services has collected samples for laboratory testing to determine the cause, with results expected to guide response actions. Officials note this is the first known incident of unknown-cause cattle deaths in the province, and there are no confirmed reports of similar cases elsewhere. Surveillance and coordinated prevention efforts continue to mitigate losses and protect livestock livelihoods.

article.articleHeadline: Fake: Tourists Massively Infected by an Unknown Virus in Vietnam.
article.articleSummary: False claim of mass infection among Russian tourists in Nha Trang, Vietnam, due to an unknown virus. No confirmed outbreak; reports cited fever and cough but tour operators and insurers denied increased patient flow. Rospotrebnadzor sent a data request to Vietnam's Ministry of Health, but that does not confirm any outbreak or novel pathogen. Media sources (TASS citing RTS, EuroIns) stated no mass complaints or diagnostic failures. Seasonal influenza remains at normal seasonal levels. Medical diagnoses reported include tonsillitis, bronchitis, laryngotracheobronchitis, pneumonia; no cases of unknown virus. Alleged infection source—dirty hotel air conditioners—was speculation by tourists and not substantiated. No information of imported/exported cases. Overall, the article debunks the rumor of mass infection; no evidence of unknown virus or diagnostic challenges observed.

article.articleHeadline: Trịnh Tường and Bát Xát hold training on the prevention and control of animal diseases.
article.articleSummary: On 9 November 2026, Lao Cai Province's Department of Plant Protection, Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services organized trainings on preventing and controlling animal diseases in Trịnh Tường and Bát Xát communes, attracting 60 participants (30 per site). In Trịnh Tường, attendees included agency representatives, party secretaries, village leaders, and livestock/veterinary workers; they received updates on livestock disease status, signs of serious infectious diseases in cattle and poultry, transmission risks, and biosecurity measures (sanitation, disinfection, vaccination, safe husbandry). In Bát Xát, 30 participants from the Commune Service Center and 25 villages learned herd management, vaccination, hygiene, reporting, and outbreak response, with emphasis on timely reporting and avoiding concealment or unsafe transport/slaughter of suspect animals. In 2026, Trịnh Tường vaccinated about 1,900 doses, mainly against rabies and foot-and-mouth disease. The trainings aim to strengthen local capacity for disease surveillance and rapid response, supporting sustainable livestock development in the region.

article.articleHeadline: Early Identification of Measles Symptoms to Proactively Prevent Outbreaks.
article.articleSummary: Measles outbreaks are increasing in Vietnam. The virus is highly contagious and spreads primarily via droplets and aerosols, and can remain airborne or on surfaces for up to two hours after an infected person leaves. A single case can infect about 20 others, and transmission occurs from roughly four days before rash onset to four days after. Early symptoms mimic influenza: high fever (39–40°C), cough, runny nose, red eyes, and fatigue; Koplik spots on the inner cheeks may appear 1–2 days before rash. The rash typically appears 3–5 days after fever starts, begins behind the ears/forehead, then spreads downward, lasting about a week with a mottled finish. Complications include pneumonia, ear infections, diarrhea, corneal ulcers, and in severe cases encephalitis or death. There is no specific antiviral therapy; management is supportive. Vaccination with two measles doses is recommended; isolate patients, use masks, inform schools and contacts, and verify immunization status.

article.articleHeadline: Influenza A case, dengue fever on the rise, hospitals forced to place extra beds in the corridors
article.articleSummary: Influenza A cases and dengue fever are rising, forcing Vietnamese hospitals to place extra beds in corridors and bolster physicians to treat severe cases. The piece emphasizes the strain on healthcare facilities and the need for heightened clinical management and staffing to handle severe influenza A and dengue fever. The information comes from VOV.VN, with no laboratory confirmation details or infection sources disclosed in the article. The date of publication is 2026-11-10, reflecting ongoing public health concerns in the country.

article.articleHeadline: Why can a person contract Dengue fever up to four times?
article.articleSummary: Vietnam reports all four dengue serotypes circulating nationwide (DENV-1 to DENV-4). From January 2026 through 10 November 2026, there have been over 170,000 suspected dengue cases and 21 deaths. Dengue is now year-round, not seasonal, due to climate change, increased rainfall, and urbanization that sustain Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. DENV-1 and DENV-2 remain predominant (about 90% of cases); DENV-3 has re-emerged after 2020–2024. Immunity to one serotype does not protect against others, allowing up to four infections per person, with sequential infections raising the risk of severe disease. Vector control is difficult because mosquitoes persist and long-running control programs waned after 2020; resource gaps at local health facilities hinder response. Surveillance tools exist, but early outbreak detection and a synchronized, multi-sector response are essential. Risk spans children, adults, and the elderly with underlying conditions.

article.articleHeadline: Agusan town logs 467 dengue cases; infection hits all 27 villages
article.articleSummary: Dengue infections in San Francisco, Agusan del Sur rise to 467 cases as of Friday, Nov 6, 2026, with transmission in all 27 villages since year start; two deaths. Teens and young adults aged 15–19 account for 88 cases (18.8%). Top barangays: Lapinigan 59, Pasta 45, 5 38, 1 32, Pisa-an 31. Others with double-digit totals include Barangay 4 (30), Karaus (29), Alegria (27), San Isidro (26), Barangay 2 (23), Bayugan 2 (23), Barangay 3 (19), Hubang (16), Borbon (11), Das-agan (11). Health Office urges continued vigilance despite no new fatalities. DOH’s enhanced 4S strategy advises searching and destroying mosquito breeding grounds, using insect repellents and protective clothing, seeking medical care at fever onset, and targeted fogging in cluster zones. Households should implement 4T routines at 4 p.m.: taob, taktak, tuyo, takip.

article.articleHeadline: Bird flu triggers imported poultry from Minnesota -- DA
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-11-09, the Philippines' Department of Agriculture imposed a temporary ban on poultry imports from Minnesota, USA after confirmed bird flu (H5N1 HPAI) outbreaks in Wright, Big Stone, Kandiyohi, Otter Tail, Becker, Ravalli, and Benton counties. The import ban covers domestic and wild birds and products (meat, day-old chicks, eggs, semen) and suspends processing/evaluation of SPSICs, revoking all approved SPSICs for Minnesota. In-transit shipments may proceed if slaughtered/processed by Aug 18. Veterinary quarantine will seize poultry exports bound for the Philippines at major ports, except for heat-treated products. The DA cites rapid HPAI spread necessitating broader restrictions; a 2016 agreement with the US allows statewide bans only if three or more counties are infected in a state. Separately, imports from Germany and Peru can resume after declaring HPAI-free; regionalization policies remain, with past restrictions on Germany (2020) and Peru (2022).

article.articleHeadline: Bogotá, rodent paradise? Signs of a pest infestation that could be gaining ground in the capital.
article.articleSummary: November 9, 2026: Bogotá faces a rodent infestation as rats and mice proliferate across the city, inhabiting waste zones and subterranean spaces, prompting health and economic concerns. Citizens and officials report increased sightings, with impacts in local commerce in areas such as the Roma neighborhood in Kennedy and other sectors. Leptospirosis is highlighted as a potential rodent-borne disease transmitted via contaminated environments; the District Health Secretariat notes rodent-related illnesses commonly present as febrile syndromes that mimic other diseases, urging medical consultation if fever follows exposure to rodents or their excreta. Urban transformation, inadequate waste management, aging infrastructure, and leaky sewers may push rodents toward settlements. Critical districts include Chapinero, Usaquén, Suba, Bosa, Engativá, and Kennedy. The issue is framed as shared responsibility under Directive 004 of 2024 among district agencies; mitigation requires waste control, infrastructure maintenance, and preventive health measures.

article.articleHeadline: Manila logs over 4,000 dengue cases from Jan. 1 to Nov. 9 | Inquirer News Manila 4,000 dengue cases
article.articleSummary: Manila reports 35 new dengue cases on Monday, Nov 9, bringing the total dengue count to 4,769 from Jan. 1 to Nov. 9, according to the Manila Health Department (MHD). Dengue remains the top-cumulative W.I.L.D. disease in EDCS-IS as of 7 a.m. on Nov. 9. On the same day, 29 new influenza-like illness (ILI) and 9 severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) cases were logged. From Jan. 1 to Nov. 9, Manila’s totals include ILI 3,009; leptospirosis 1,664; SARI 631; COVID-19 115; typhoid fever 91; and cholera 4. No new cases of cholera, typhoid fever, confirmed COVID-19 or leptospirosis were reported on Monday. MHD’s W.I.L.D. surveillance covers waterborne diseases, influenza, leptospirosis and dengue, and also tracks ILI, SARI and confirmed COVID-19. Residents are urged to prevent water accumulation, keep surroundings clean, drink clean water, and seek medical attention if symptoms appear during the rainy season.

article.articleHeadline: SAFETYNET Expands Field Epidemiology Training and Disease Surveillance
article.articleSummary: SAFETYNET, a Philippines-based NGO supporting applied epidemiology since 2009, expanded operations in India from March 2018 to December 2024, partnering under CDC's Global Health Security Agenda to build field epidemiology capacity. By 2024 it supported 28 training cohorts across India, assisting over 110 outbreak investigations, more than 70 surveillance evaluations, and 14 epidemiological research studies. The three-tier program—frontline (3 months), intermediate (12–18 months), and advanced (24 months)—was delivered through MoHFW-approved MoUs with NCDC, ICMR-NIE Chennai, NIHFW, NIPHTR Mumbai, WHO India, and others; trainees worked in New Delhi, Mumbai, and Chennai, with 124 districts in eight states reached for frontline training. During COVID-19, 98% of active trainees and 86% of alumni engaged in emergency response (cluster investigations, screening, contact tracing, containment). Outcomes included mass gathering surveillance, heat-related fatality autopsy protocols, a national COVID-19 facility preparedness tool, and writing workshops yielding 64 manuscripts and 180 conference abstracts; four grants were secured.

article.articleHeadline: (Multimedia) China and Africa strengthen their cooperation in the fight against infectious diseases.
article.articleSummary: During 6–7 November 2026 in Guangzhou, the first China–Africa Forum on Public Health announced a joint initiative by the Chinese CDC and Africa CDC to strengthen cooperation against infectious diseases, boosting prevention, surveillance, and outbreak response through shared expertise, technical support, and local training. The partnership covers Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of Congo and expanded malaria and schistosomiasis control, including practical lab capacity building at the DRC’s INRB that improved diagnostic sensitivity and specificity. Malaria programs yield major gains: Comoros achieved near-elimination with 2017 deaths zero; in Tanzania, rapid, community-based screening cut infections from 36.88% to 5.38% in pilots and influenced WHO scaling to Burkina Faso, Senegal, and Zambia. Zimbabwe’s schistosomiasis efforts started in 2020, with 2023 training of 50 technicians and surveys of 399 households across 14 villages (1,358 samples). Li Shizhu highlights shared elimination experiences; Deng Huihong stresses mutual learning.

article.articleHeadline: How Ghana can prepare for possible Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: Ghana should intensify public education, widen dissemination of information on quarantine and isolation facilities, strengthen case-management preparedness, and bolster surveillance across agencies to ready for a possible Ebola outbreak. Speaking on the 68th GMA Annual General Conference, Prof. Yorke urged moving beyond routine entry-point surveillance to enhance community-level monitoring, designate quarantine and isolation sites, and proactively allocate funds to finance response efforts. He called on the public to maintain good hygiene and observe preventive measures, and to avoid physical contact with suspected or confirmed Ebola cases, infected bodies, and contaminated objects. While commending the Ministry of Health and the Ghana Health Service, he said additional measures are needed to protect the country. The reported detection of the Bundibugyo strain in Nigeria should heighten preparedness for cross-border transmission; Ghana has announced new travel rules for arriving passengers.
